thread:
ops-bot: ALERT: continuous-batcher queue growth detected in us-west-2 production cluster (cluster-a). token-latency spike, several containers OOM killed. paging observed on host nodes. auto-page = true :rotating_light:
incident-bot: SEV2 triggered by latency > 800ms for 15m, affected routes: /generate, /chat. Notifying oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batcher-paging
oncall_jess: seeing it. I'm on it. oncall -> eng-runtime handoff. 
oncall_jess: customer reports? csm_amy?
csm_amy: AcmePay reported errors in checkout flows ~08:42 PDT, high latency and 502s. They've opened a ticket and want ETA.
infra_kim: node-flip alerts across 3 GPU hosts, some nodes marked NotReady by k8s due to OOM events (oom_kill). Host paging I/O very high.
dev_runtime_max: logs show repeated CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY and container restarts from OOM killer; but also large batch accumulators kept growing (accumulator_size >> expected). Suspect continuous-batcher leak in accumulation logic.
sre_lead_raj: any customer impact footprint? which regions?
csm_amy: AcmePay is US-west primary; some EU customers saw elevated latency but no 502s yet.
oncall_jess: ok prioritizing AcmePay impact. Dev + infra on the call. What's the quickest mitigation? throttle batching or kill accumulator?
dev_runtime_max: we can flip emergency throttle on the runtime layer to cap max_accumulator_bytes to 256MB, and reduce max_batch_delay to 5ms to force smaller batches. That should drop throughput but reduce tail latency.
infra_kim: prepping k8s patch to set env var BATCHER_MAX_ACCUM_BYTES=268435456 on workload. Will push to cluster-a only. Need approval to rollout to prod via hotpatch.
oncall_jess: approved. Do it. Notify before patch.
infra_kim: patch applied to 6 pods on cluster-a. Rolling restart in progress. kubectl commands: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher BATCHER_MAX_ACCUM_BYTES=268435456 -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher -n prod
```
ops-bot: rollback window 15m. Auto-scaling suspended for that deployment during patch.
dev_runtime_max: also enabling prefix/KV cache eviction policy (evict-oldest=true) to avoid KV cache growth that's causing host swap. Command below: 
```
PATCH /config/runtime HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
{ "kv_cache.eviction_policy": "evict-oldest" }
```
sre_lead_raj: after restart, one pod shows healthier memory usage but we still see CUDA OOM on a specific GPU on node gpu-07. Suspect partial GPU memory leak on model variant xlarge-quant.
infra_kim: isolating node gpu-07, draining to avoid further flips: `kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
ops-bot: Node gpu-07 cordon + drain started. Expected 30s per pod to reschedule.
customer_acme_oncall: thanks, we see decreased failures on our side. continue updates please.
oncall_jess: good. we're seeing p50 drop from 920ms to 320ms after patch. p99 still high ~1.5s.
dev_runtime_max: to reduce p99 we can temporarily route heavy traffic to dedicated capacity (reserved) where batching uses smaller default accumulator, and fallback to smaller model variant for long-tail requests. Running routing change now: 
```
POST /admin/routing/update
{ "route_filter": "customer:AcmePay", "target_pool": "dedicated-east-01" }
```
ops-bot: routing change applied for AcmePay. Confirmed by control-plane.
sre_lead_raj: tracking root cause: continuous-batcher accumulator growth on specific request patterns (large context + streaming). Need reproduction. Max, can you reproduce on staging with long streaming sessions?
dev_runtime_max: yes, I have a reproducer. I can exercise accumulator growth with concurrent streaming of long-prefix prompts. Will file a bug and patch.
oncall_jess: for now, keep emergency throttle live and routing to dedicated for affected customers. How long to stabilize?
infra_kim: nodes stabilized, no new OOM kills in last 7 minutes. Host swap I/O down 70%.
csm_amy: AcmePay confirms checkout is back to normal for most customers, a few slow sessions remain but no errors. They want a postmortem and timeline.
sre_lead_raj: assign postmortem to eng-runtime + infra. Max to lead root-cause analysis. Raj will own mitigation plan. Jess will coordinate customer comms.
dev_runtime_max: filing bug: CR-2026: continuous-batcher accumulator not bounded for streaming + long-prefix; reproduction + initial fix attached.
incident-bot: ACTIONS: (1) emergency throttle applied (BATCHER_MAX_ACCUM_BYTES=256MB) (2) KV cache eviction policy enabled (evict-oldest) (3) Isolated node gpu-07 and drained (4) Routed AcmePay to dedicated pool. All mitigations active.
oncall_jess: good job team. keeping channel open for 1 hour for watch. If p99 < 900ms for 30m we'll close.
dev_runtime_max: note: logs show CUDA stacktrace in one crashed pod: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 26.10 GiB already allocated)
  File "/app/runtime/batcher.py", line 842, in process_batch
    kv_cache.extend(prefix_kv)
```
sre_lead_raj: include regression tests for streaming long-prefix cases and add telemetry: accumulator_size gauge and alert when > 128MB per pod.
csm_amy: looping back to AcmePay with ETA for fix and postmortem.
oncall_jess: closing note: customer impact contained, mitigations in place, root-cause assigned. Will update timeline and postmortem link once created. Thanks. :pray:
ops-bot: Incident SEV2 -> degraded -> mitigated. Closing watch window at 3234509988.
